deck_title: Malus-Brewster I = I0*cos^2(phi) = I0/(1+tan^2(phi)) polarizer extinction law vs naive scalar unpolarized glare rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Étienne-Louis Malus (1809) & Sir David Brewster (1815) linear polarizer cosine-squared extinction law (projecting the electric field vector as E_trans = E_0 * cos(phi) so transmitted irradiance scales as I(phi) = I_0 * cos^2(phi) = I_0 / (1 + tan^2(phi)) = I_0 / (1 + u), locking I_active / I_Malus = 1.0000x across all 17 stations u = tan^2(phi) in [0.000, 1.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive scalar unpolarized intensity shader (I = I_0, which leaks excess glare irradiance by sec^2(phi) = 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-slice optical cycle Poynting E^2(t) quadrature.
